content: Pyuria is a medical condition characterized by the presence of 10 or more white blood cells per cubic millimeter (mm³) in a urine sample. This condition may also present with a positive Gram stain and/or a positive leukocyte esterase test on a urinary dipstick. Pyuria can be indicative of various underlying conditions, including bacterial or non-bacterial urinary tract infections, genitourinary abnormalities, inflammatory disorders, or systemic diseases. It is important to note that pyuria itself does not require treatment; however, the underlying cause must be identified and appropriately managed. The definition of pyuria includes the following criteria: The presence of 10 or more white blood cells per mm³ in a urine specimen. A positive Gram stain result from an unspun urine sample. A positive leukocyte esterase result on a urinary dipstick test. Pyuria can be classified into two categories based on the presence or absence of detectable infection: 1. Sterile pyuria (absence of detectable infection). 2. Bacteriuria (presence of detectable infection). To differentiate between the various diseases that may cause pyuria, a thorough differential diagnosis is required. For sterile pyuria, specific diagnostic considerations must be reviewed to identify the underlying etiology.
